diagnostic.root_cause: Race time regression 16.97→23.0s caused by conservative L-BFGS time allocation across 25 segments (doubled from 14). Tracking error now excellent (avg 0.186m) but drone flies too slowly. Speed optimization is the critical next step.
architectural_issues: 25 trajectory segments (entry/exit per gate) causes overly conservative time allocation
L-BFGS optimizer spreads time too evenly across segments — needs stronger speed bias
Controller still saturates at 0.7 rad tilt limit, preventing sharper turns at higher speed
Gate-6 slight regression (+0.034m) from helix entry transition waypoint placement
critic_findings: Race time increased 35% — dual waypoints improved accuracy but at severe speed cost
Minimum segment time (0.1s) may be too permissive for L-BFGS — try providing speed-aware initial guess
Consider making entry/exit offset adaptive based on approach angle rather than fixed 0.4m

improvements_backlog.description: Race time 23.0s → target 14s: time allocation is far too conservative with 25 segments
improvements_backlog.proposed_approach: Increase speed factors in _initial_time_allocation (0.65→0.80 for straights, 0.55→0.70 for turns, 0.45→0.55 for sharp turns). Also reduce entry/exit segment time allocation since 0.8m segments should be fast. Alternatively, provide velocity constraints to L-BFGS to prevent excessive slowdown.
improvements_backlog.expected_impact: Race time reduction 23→16s, possibly 14s with aggressive tuning

improvements_backlog.description: Increase max tilt limit from 0.7 to 0.8 rad to allow more aggressive turns
improvements_backlog.proposed_approach: Increase max_tilt_angle in DroneConstraints and TrackerConfig. Allows controller to track tighter turns at higher speed.
improvements_backlog.expected_impact: Enables higher speed through turns without accuracy loss

improvements_backlog.description: Entry/exit offset could be adaptive (shorter for gentle approaches, longer for sharp turns)
improvements_backlog.proposed_approach: Scale the 0.4m offset by turn angle: 0.2m for straight approaches, 0.5m for sharp turns
improvements_backlog.expected_impact: Reduce total trajectory length, improve gate-6 regression

improvements_backlog.description: Install gym-pybullet-drones and enable PyBullet benchmark path
improvements_backlog.proposed_approach: pip install gym-pybullet-drones, enable simulation section in benchmark
improvements_backlog.expected_impact: More realistic benchmarking with real physics

improvements_backlog.description: Integrate GateTracker/GatePnP/EKF into runner for perception filtering
improvements_backlog.proposed_approach: Port perception modules from race_pipeline.py into sim_pybullet runner
improvements_backlog.expected_impact: Eliminate raw detection target jumps in PyBullet sim

failed_approaches.description: Increased max_velocity from 10.0 to 12.0 AND initial time allocation from 0.6 to 0.7 simultaneously. Trajectory became too aggressive for kinematic sim PD controller — max tracking error jumped to 6.4m and gate pass rate dropped to 67%.
failed_approaches.lesson: Match trajectory aggressiveness to controller capability. Change one parameter at a time.

failed_approaches.description: Curvature-aware initial time allocation had no measurable impact because L-BFGS optimizer in _optimize_time_allocation re-optimizes times regardless of initial guess.
failed_approaches.lesson: Initial time allocation heuristic matters less than the optimizer that runs after it. Focus on optimizer constraints or objective function changes rather than initialization.
failed_approaches.metrics_delta: No measurable change in any metric
